work_order.confidence_rationale: The defect is a property of two string constants, so I could settle it without a browser: I extracted the two MESSAGE templates from the installed node_modules/@radix-ui/react-dialog@1.1.15, rebuilt the concrete strings, and ran them against the shipped pattern, the dbcdcee-broken pattern, and the proposed fix. The shipped probe reaches only the description arm; the proposed two-probe set plus the coverage assertion catches both single-arm mutations. Both proposed probe strings are byte-exact transcriptions of the installed dist, and the title warning goes to console.error while the description warning goes to console.warn, which is why the fix tags each probe with its channel. What I did NOT do is run Playwright myself: node_modules was absent at the start of this session and a real run needs a live preview server, so the poll's timing behaviour is reasoned about rather than observed. QA measured CDP console delivery at 102-105ms against the 1000ms timeout with 9/9 green including 3 runs under CPU saturation, which is why I am not treating that as open risk. Also unverified by me: that the repo's e2e lint/typecheck stays clean after the edit, and that the implementer's sandbox can start the dev server to run the control runs.
work_order.debate_summary:
The question this revision turns on is whether the previous attempt was a bad fix or a bad specification, and the evidence says specification. The plan asked for one probe string against a regex with two alternatives, and wrote an acceptance criterion whose mutation step touched only one of them. The implementer delivered exactly that, and the two comments that over-claim are the ones the plan told it to write. So the revision does not patch the comment, does not add a second comment, and does not re-roll the same probe with better wording: it changes the shape of the check. Two probes instead of one, each tagged with the console channel Radix actually uses for it, plus a static assertion that fails by name when a filter alternative has no probe — which is the property the original plan assumed and never specified. I verified the whole construction against the installed @radix-ui/react-dialog@1.1.15 rather than against the doc comment, so the transcriptions are byte-exact and the console-channel difference is captured rather than assumed.

One criterion moves, and I would rather be explicit about it than let it read as a quiet relaxation. AC-2 named a constant that the fix necessarily renames, so leaving it verbatim would hand the next QA run a criterion that fails correct code. It keeps its id, its position, its drain timing, its how_to_verify procedure and its caveat that the probe does not prove Radix still emits these strings; the only change is singular to plural, and `understanding` quotes the before and after so a reviewer can check the claim moved and the bar did not. Everything else — AC-1 to AC-9 — is carried forward verbatim, and AC-10 and AC-11 are added after them for the arm nobody mutated and for the control that proves it.

The two things a human still has to do, the missing [AI] prefix on the PR title and the reviewer's note-category point, are named in risks and out_of_scope rather than folded in. The title cannot be fixed from this loop at all: the implementer has no token that can push, comment or label, and the pipeline owns the string it generated.
work_order.understanding:
QA found one blocking bug on PR #60, BUG-1, and everything else passed: 18 tests, all four control mutations reproduced independently, the full command-bar file 3/3, lint and e2e typecheck clean, release note valid, tree restored byte-identical. This revision changes one test file and nothing else.

THE PREVIOUS PLAN WAS WRONG, AND THE IMPLEMENTER WAS NOT. The plan specified a self-checking probe as a single constant — 'Add a module-level `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE` holding Radix's verbatim description-warning string' — and described what it bought as 'the filter still matches the transcribed Radix wording'. That sentence treats `dialogAccessibilityWarning` as one thing. It is not: it is an alternation of two Radix messages, one about a missing `DialogTitle` and one about a missing `Description`. A test can only re-probe what it emits, so a single probe string re-proves one of the two alternatives and leaves the other unobservable. The plan's own AC-2 was written the same way — its how_to_verify says to mutate 'for example delete the `Missing .Description. or .aria-describedby` alternative', naming only the description arm, so no check in the plan could ever have distinguished the arms. The implementer built exactly what the plan asked for, and the comments that over-claim are the comments the plan told it to write ('an edit that breaks the match turns this test red on every run'). So this is a defect in the specification, not a slip in the execution, and patching the comment instead of the probe would have preserved the wrong premise. I am not doing that, and the approach below is a different shape, not the same one described more carefully: two probes instead of one, a static assertion that makes the coverage property itself enforced, and control evidence for the arm nobody had mutated.

I REPRODUCED IT MYSELF, AT THE LEVEL THE DEFECT LIVES. The shipped probe string matches the description alternative and not the title alternative, and a pattern with the title arm narrowed to the exact broken form dbcdcee shipped (`DialogContent requires a DialogTitle`, no `.` standing in for Radix's backticks) still matches the probe — so the whole test stays green. That is QA's mutation reproduced from the constants rather than from their run, and it is what makes `reproduced: true` honest. I also confirmed against the installed package that the shipped pattern does still match the real title message today, so this is a coverage blind spot and an overstated comment, not a live regression — exactly as QA filed it.

ONE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS EDITED IN PLACE, AND HERE IS EXACTLY WHAT CHANGED. AC-2 named `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE` and described it as proving 'filter match' for the pattern as a whole. The fix renames that constant to a plural array, so AC-2 as written would name a symbol the corrected code does not have, and QA — which gets the criteria and deliberately no memory of last run — would fail a change that did the right thing. AC-2 keeps its id, its position, its drain timing, its 'the probe proves channel delivery and filter match; it does not prove Radix's current build emits that exact string' caveat and its how_to_verify procedure. The only change is singular to plural: 'emits DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE' becomes 'emits one probe message per alternative the filter contains', and 'that exact message' becomes 'that message'. The bar is not lowered — it is stated one level up, where it was always meant to sit. Nothing is renumbered and nothing is dropped. AC-10 and AC-11 are new, numbered after AC-9, and they cover what BUG-1 exposed rather than what AC-2 already said.

TWO THINGS QA RAISED THAT THIS WORK ORDER CANNOT FIX, both flagged rather than silently dropped. The PR title is 'fix: Follow-ups from #48: 7 from the review' with no `[AI]` prefix, against .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md, and because GitHub's squash merge reuses the title as the commit subject, main gets an unprefixed commit. That is a one-word edit on a pull request, and nothing here can make it: the implementer runs with a read-only token that cannot push, comment or label. Same for the reviewer's separate finding that the note's category should be Maintenance rather than Bugfix — AC-8 pins `category: Bugfix`, the check accepts it, and it belongs to the follow-up ticket the pipeline already opened rather than to a revision that would have to rewrite a passed criterion to change it. Both are in risks/out_of_scope so they are decisions in front of a human, not surprises at merge.
work_order.root_cause: The test's self-check and the filter it guards have different shapes. `dialogAccessibilityWarning` is an alternation of two Radix messages — a missing `DialogTitle` and a missing `Description` — while `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE` is a single string constant holding one of them. A test can only re-probe what it emits, so the title alternative is never exercised: editing it to the exact form dbcdcee shipped, one that cannot match Radix's real backticked message, leaves the whole suite green while the constant's doc comment and the inline block both claim that an edit breaking the match turns the test red on every run. The original work order created that asymmetry by specifying one probe string and by writing an acceptance criterion that mutated only the description alternative, so neither the plan nor any automated stage could have distinguished the two arms.

files.change: Delete the `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE` constant and its doc comment, and replace them with a `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBES` array plus an explicit element type: two entries, `{ channel: 'error', message: '`DialogContent` requires a `DialogTitle` for the component to be accessible for screen reader users.' }` and `{ channel: 'warn', message: 'Warning: Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby={undefined}` for {DialogContent}.' }`. Both strings are transcribed from the installed @radix-ui/react-dialog@1.1.15 — the title message is only the first line of Radix's three-paragraph warning — and the `error`/`warn` tags record the console channel Radix emits each on, because `watchDialogWarnings` only collects console types `error` and `warning` and Radix uses one of each. Give the array an explicit element type rather than `as const`, so it stays assignable to `page.evaluate`'s serialisable parameter. In the test body, replace the single-probe block with two things, in this order. First, a static coverage assertion before anything is emitted: iterate `dialogAccessibilityWarning.source.split('|')` and assert, with a custom message naming the alternative, that `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBES.some(({ message }) => new RegExp(alternative).test(message))` is true — so adding a third alternative to the filter fails the test by name until a third probe exists; comment that the naive `split('|')` is correct for this flat alternation and would need revisiting if the pattern gained a group or an escaped `|`. Second, the emission: keep `const probe = watchDialogWarnings(page);` and the probe's position after `expect(messages).toEqual([])`, then `await page.evaluate(probes => { for (const { channel, message } of probes) { if (channel === 'error') { console.error(message); } else { console.warn(message); } } }, DIALOG_WARNING_PROBES);` followed by `await expect.poll(() => [...probe.messages].sort(), { timeout: CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS }).toEqual(DIALOG_WARNING_PROBES.map(({ message }) => message).sort());` — both sides sorted, because CDP does not guarantee the order of two console events and an order-sensitive assertion would be a flake; equality rather than `includes` so the collector is also proven to hold each message exactly once. Rewrite the constant's doc comment and the inline block above the probe so they claim what is now true — every alternative in the filter has its own probe and is re-proved on every run, and the coverage assertion fails if one has none — while keeping the honest limit that this does not prove Radix's current build emits these strings. Leave the `dialogAccessibilityWarning` doc comment unchanged: it keeps the `@radix-ui/react-dialog@1.1.15` pin and both verbatim messages and cites no line numbers. Leave `reports.test.ts` and the release note alone.

The fix changes the probe from one message to one-per-alternative, records the console channel Radix actually uses for each, and adds the static assertion that makes the coverage property enforced rather than asserted in a comment — so the blind spot QA proved by mutation cannot come back with the next alternative.

risks: PR #60's title is 'fix: Follow-ups from #48: 7 from the review' with no `[AI]` prefix, against .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md, and GitHub's squash merge reuses the title as the commit subject — so main gets an unprefixed commit unless a human edits the title while the PR is open. No agent in this loop can do it: the implementer runs with a read-only token that cannot push, comment or label, and the pipeline owns the title it generated. This is a one-word edit by a person and it blocks a clean merge independently of everything in this work order.

The coverage assertion splits the pattern source on `|` and compiles each fragment. That is exact for this flat two-way alternation and would be wrong for a pattern containing a group or an escaped `|`. The comment says so at the call site. It fails loudly and by name if the pattern grows, which is the safe direction, but a future change that adds a group has to revisit it — recorded here rather than left for the next reader to discover.

The probe now emits two console events instead of one, so there are two CDP round-trips inside the same CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS rather than one. QA measured console delivery at 102-105ms against the 1000ms timeout over 12 samples and ran the test 9 times, 3 under deliberate CPU saturation on 4 cores, with no timeout; two events do not change that headroom materially. If a loaded machine ever does exceed it, the failure is a correct-and-loud flake rather than a vacuous pass, which is the trade this design accepts.

Both probe strings are transcriptions of `@radix-ui/react-dialog@1.1.15` held in the test file, and the package floats on `^1.1.6`. If a patch release rewords either message, the coverage assertion still passes — it checks the probes against the pattern, not against the installed package — and the filter would stop matching the real warning while the test stayed green. That limit is unchanged from the previous attempt and is stated in the constant's comment rather than papered over; closing it would mean reading the package's dist at test time, which is a larger design change than this revision should make.

The title probe emits only the first line of Radix's three-paragraph title warning. That is deliberate — the filter matches inside that line and the rest is developer-facing prose — but it means the probe is not byte-identical to the full string Radix logs. Both are recorded in the constant's comment so nobody later 'fixes' the truncation into a mismatch.

Every run of the command-bar test spends ~1s of unconditional wall clock on the drain that #39 did not, plus the probe's poll. This is the price the review accepted; the removed race only ever hid it on green runs.

The release note credits Shivam-Fl, a human, because findNonPersonAuthors hard-rejects `claude`, `github-actions` and any `[bot]` handle. That matches dbcdcee for the previous change to this same file, but if the human who merges disagrees about attribution that is a one-line edit to the front matter, called out here so it is a decision rather than a surprise in the changelog.

No forbidden_path is touched: the only edited file is packages/desktop-client/e2e/command-bar.test.ts. .sdlc/config.yml is left alone, so verify.e2e stays empty and no automated stage will run these tests — which is why AC-2, AC-10 and AC-11 all name the exact command QA must run rather than citing CI. The implementer does not write the PR body and does not commit implementer-reply.md.

No host outside env.api_allowlist is contacted by the change itself; I fetched @radix-ui/react-dialog@1.1.15 from unpkg only to verify the two transcriptions, and the implementer should read them from node_modules instead.

evidence: BUG-1 reproduced directly, from the constants rather than from QA's run. Against PR #60's shipped `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE` and shipped pattern /DialogContent. requires a .DialogTitle|Missing .Description. or .aria-describedby/: the probe matches the description alternative (true) and does NOT match the title alternative (false). Narrowing only the title arm to dbcdcee's shipped broken form and re-testing the probe still yields a match, so the whole test stays green — QA's mutation, reconstructed from the strings.

Both proposed probe strings are byte-exact transcriptions of the installed package, not of the doc comment. `node -p "require('./node_modules/@radix-ui/react-dialog/package.json').version"` → 1.1.15. `sed -n '288p;304p' node_modules/@radix-ui/react-dialog/dist/index.mjs` gives the title MESSAGE template and the description template. Substituting DialogContent/DialogTitle yields exactly the two strings in files[].change. This also confirms AC-5's removed line numbers (288 and 304) were accurate for the pinned version — they were dropped for rot, not for being wrong.

The two Radix warnings go to different console channels, which is why the probes are tagged: the title warning is emitted by `console.error(MESSAGE)` and the description warning by `console.warn(MESSAGE)` in that same dist. `watchDialogWarnings` collects only console types `error` and `warning`, so emitting both probes through one method would under-test the collector's type guard.

The two probe messages are disjoint against the filter — the title message matches only the title arm and the description message only the description arm — so a failure localises to one arm rather than to either.

The proposed fix catches both mutations, checked against the real strings: with the title arm narrowed to `DialogContent requires a DialogTitle`, the coverage assertion flags that alternative as unprobed by name and the poll collects 1 of 2 probes; with the description arm narrowed to `MissingZZ .Description. or .aria-describedby`, the same happens for that arm. review.detail:
The probe re-proves one of `dialogAccessibilityWarning`'s two alternatives, and the one it skips is the one that has actually broken in this file's history. `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE` holds only the description warning, so `expect.poll(...).toEqual([DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE])` exercises the `Missing .Description. or .aria-describedby` arm and never the `DialogContent. requires a .DialogTitle` arm. The probe's own comments — the constant's doc comment ("the filter still matches the transcribed wording") and the inline block ("an edit that breaks the match turns this test red on every run") — both read as claims about the whole pattern, so a future narrowing of the title arm would leave the probe green while its documentation says otherwise. dbcdcee's second commit in this file was exactly that bug: the shipped pattern had a bare space where Radix's backtick sits, so the title arm could not match, and only the description alternative fired. That is the failure the probe exists to catch, and it is the arm the probe is blind to.

`packages/desktop-client/e2e/command-bar.test.ts:32`

Evidence: `const DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE = 'Warning: Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby={undefined}` for {DialogContent}.'` at :32-33. The pattern at :21 is `/DialogContent. requires a .DialogTitle|Missing .Description. or .aria-describedby/`. Running both strings against both arms: `alt1.test(probe) === false`, `alt2.test(probe) === true`, `alt1.test(titleMsg) === true`, `alt2.test(titleMsg) === false` — the probe reaches exactly one arm. The title arm's regression history is recorded in dbcdcee's own message: "Radix's title message reads `DialogContent` requires a `DialogTitle` ... — a backtick sits between DialogContent and ' requires', so the pattern shipped with a bare space there could not match it. Only the description alternative fired." The work order's own AC-2 verification mutates only the description alternative ("for example delete the `Missing .Description. or .aria-describedby` alternative"), so neither the check nor the comment distinguishes the two arms.

Fix: Either widen the probe to emit both messages and assert `expect.poll(...).toEqual([TITLE_PROBE, DESC_PROBE])` — or, if a second emitted warning is not wanted, derive the probe constants from the two quoted messages in the doc comment so the regex, the comment, and the probe cannot drift apart. Failing both, narrow the two comments to say "the description arm" rather than "the filter", so the code does not claim coverage it does not have.
